$comment: 14 §6 🔒: 'a build-time check enumerates every 📐 marker in the documentation set against
the schema keys and fails on a mismatch. That check is what stops the tuning surface eroding
An exact 1:1 match is not reachable today and pretending otherwise would mean weakening the
check. This file is the honest alternative: every mismatch that exists right now, each with a
reason and the milestone that closes it. The check FAILS on anything not recorded here, and
equally on an entry here that no longer describes a real mismatch — so the file can only
shrink without somebody arguing for it in a diff. It is a measurement of spec debt, not a
unmatchedMarkers        — a 📐 marker in game-design/ whose doc section no schema key cites.
unmarkedSchemaCitations — a NUMERIC key in a tuning/ schema whose cited doc section carries
no 📐 marker. The tuning surface eroding from the other side.
closedBy names the milestone task that removes the entry, or the literal 'never' where the
marker is not a tunable at all (a glossary row, a prose reference to the rule itself). 'never'
is deliberately conspicuous: there are four of them and each one should be argued with.
Regenerate the SHAPE with:  dotnet run --project tools/ContentValidator -- --write-baseline
then write the reasons by hand. A generated reason is not a reason.

unmatchedMarkers.reason: The glossary row that defines the 📐 marker itself. It is documentation about the rule, not a number.
Launch content counts (90 perks, 8 chapters, ...). Identity of the content set, authored as files under content/, not as a tuning key.
Run and animation durations. Presentation timing, owned by the client; 21 sweeps nothing in it.
Campfire heal percentage. Belongs in the board-tile content that M2 authors under content/board_events/.
Board topology: nodes per stage, fork count, fork length. Board generation is M2-03; the keys land in the chapter content schema, not in tuning/.
The Portal jump range 3-6. A board-generation constant, authored with the board generator.
The TILE_CACHE egg rate. 03 §7a.4 owns the payout table and IS matched; this is the same number quoted in the tile-type table.
Chapter signature mechanics (Burning tile share, Clockwork pressure). Per-chapter content, authored under content/chapters/.
Minigame reward tables per chapter. currencies.json holds minigameRewards but the per-chapter split is unauthored.
Dice reroll charges per stage. The dice system is M1-05; no tuning key exists yet.
The die-face weighting constants (0.55 / 0.12 / clamps). Same owner as §3.
Dice animation timings and Fast Mode. Presentation, owned by the client.
The combat caps. 16 A7 rules these balance rather than economy: they live in combat_caps.json under content/, outside tuning/ by design.
The BLEED missing-HP scaling term. A status-effect parameter, authored with the effect DSL content.
Enemy archetype rows live in enemies.json (content identity, not economy). No schema exists for it yet.
Enemy level per (chapter, tier). 29 §4-5 owns par_power.json but the level table itself is unauthored there.
Archetype secondary stat columns. enemies.json, as §6.
The WARDEN SUNDER parameter set and the per-chapter CASTER status rows. enemies.json.
Elite modifier assignments. enemies.json.
Chapter enemy-pool weights. Authored per chapter under content/chapters/.
The perk count (90 standard). Content identity; the perks themselves are content/perks/.
Codex mastery bonuses (+17.2% all stats). Perk-collection content, authored with the Codex.
Pet ability values. beasts.json holds the level/egg economy; the per-pet abilities are content/pets/.
Mount stat blocks and run perks. content/mounts/.
The free talent-preset allowance. A UX allowance the doc says to raise on telemetry, not an economy dial the simulator sweeps.
A verification instruction ('verify with the balance harness'), not a number that lives in a file.
The paragraph describing the simulator's role. Prose about 📐 numbers, not a 📐 number.
The PvP loadout Perk Point budget. PvP tuning has no file in the 21 §3.1 catalogue; M6 decides whether it joins currencies.json or gets its own key.
PvP attempt refresh time. Same owner as §3.
Matchmaking rating band and widening. Same owner as §3.
JWT access and refresh lifetimes. Server configuration, not game content: it never reaches a ContentSnapshot.
A decision-log row quoting in-run economy numbers that currencies.json already owns. The log has no numbered sections, so the citation join cannot reach it.
Boss mechanic tunables. content/bosses/ is M3 work and has no schema yet.
The FTUE script's tutorial-only full heal. ftue.json is a sequencing file, not economy; 19 has no numbered sections for the join to bind to.
The sentence stating this very rule. Prose about the check, not a number.
The standard-chest pity ladder. luck.json holds hardPity and softPity, but the schema key cites 24 §4.2 rather than §4.1, so the join misses by one section.
An instruction that counter strings are localisation keys and must be width-tested in German. Not a number.
An art-budget line (three dungeon-select illustrations). Not a tunable at all; it sits in the asset manifest.
The account-link one-time grant (500 Soul Shards + a chest). Belongs in currencies.json's earn sources; 28 has no numbered sections for the join.

unmarkedSchemaCitations.reason: forge.json crownCostByOutputRarity cites 08 §4.1, whose 📐 marker sits in §4 (the Forge header) — the join is one level off, not absent.
forge.json stoneCostPerLevel cites 08 §4.2. 08 §4's 📐 marker covers it; the section granularity differs.
forge.json inventory/maxCapacity cites 08 §5, which states the 400 cap in prose without a 📐 marker — the same section 16 A7 flags as conflicting with 10 §4.
beasts.json eggOdds cites 24 §4.4 (egg pity). 24's 📐 markers sit in §4.1 and §9; §4.4 itself carries none.
forge.json stoneCostPerLevel carries 25 §7's E9 instruction to re-derive the +11..+15 costs by simulation. An instruction, not a marked tunable.
progression.json unlocks cites 26 §5 for the EVENTS gate. 26 carries one 📐 marker and it is elsewhere.
par_power.json tooWeakWarningRatio cites 29 §4.2. 29's markers are in §2-3 and §6; §4.2 states the warning ratio without one.
